method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18; a date module (cor-dates.l4, built-in date functions only), a seat-neutral core (cor-core.l4) and one seat layer (the family member) that restates no rule; answers are named outcomes, booleans for definitions and 'if' conditions, numbers and dates; no MAYBE BOOLEAN, so no NOTHING-kind tags; one regulative rule (the s 27(3) appeal time limit, run with EVALTRACE over plain dates); no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Coroners Act 2003 (SA), register version 31.1.2023, fetched from www.legislation.sa.gov.au on 2026-11-06 (unauthorised RTF; not the Open Australian Legal Corpus), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/coroners-act-2003.txt (text sha256 3f59a470259453188d9c042b02d5533954b88660b9cd4648dbb1bf2109754e3d per its meta.json). The Coroners Regulations and the Coroner's Court rules are not deposited; what they set (excluded procedures, prescribed circumstances, s 37 classes and fees, the s 29(2)(c) consent form, the s 20A(4)(b) nomination) is asked as facts. The uncommenced 2025 amendment is not incorporated.
license: Apache-2.0 for the L4; the quoted statutory text is South Australian legislation, CC BY 4.0 (State of South Australia); see SOURCE-LICENSE.md
seat: the family member: the relative of a person who has died or disappeared in South Australia, who meets the coronial process and may later bring or answer a claim about the death; also, as the same individual, the person who must report a death (s 28), a witness at the inquest (ss 23, 23A), and a person whose interests or competence a finding touches (s 27) (cor-seat.l4)
